key_insight: Weakened stratification drives a clear progression from buoyancy-dominated shear flow to Kelvin--Helmholtz-enhanced mixing and then to near-isotropic turbulence, with VSHFs and anisotropic spectral steepening emerging in the intermediate regime.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict when stratified shear will amplify mixing and intermittency, which is important for geophysical flows, plume transport, and mixing-control models.
method: Direct numerical simulations of stably stratified Kolmogorov-forced shear flow
Parameter sweep across a broad range of Froude numbers to vary stratification strength
Analysis of energy spectra, spectral fluxes, intermittency statistics, and mixing coefficients
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regime transitions, negative large-scale perpendicular fluxes from anisotropic redistribution, strong non-Gaussian vertical-velocity kurtosis at high stratification, and mixing coefficients remaining around 10^-1 with modest KH-related enhancement.
watch_item: The apparent upscale perpendicular flux is not a true inverse cascade, so interpretation must distinguish anisotropic redistribution from net energy transfer reversal.
paper_title: Energy transfer, Intermittency and Mixing in Shear-Driven Stratified Turbulence
